text: In Plantinga's modal ontological argument, which single premise carries the entire disputed weight, so that granting it yields God's existence in S5?
choices: The premise that a maximally great being, if it exists in any possible world, exists in every possible world—which follows directly from building necessary existence into maximal greatness.
The premise that it is possible that a maximally great being exists—that the concept is coherent and instantiated in at least one possible world.
The modal principle that whatever is necessary is actual, taking us from necessary existence to actual existence.
The premise that existence is a perfection which, added to the concept of the greatest conceivable being, entails that it exists.
explanation: The whole burden falls on P1, mere possibility; once it is granted, the S5 axiom (possibly-necessarily P entails necessarily P) converts possible necessary existence into actual necessary existence. Option 0 states the uncontroversial P2, which just unpacks the definition of maximal greatness; option 3 is the Anselmian/Cartesian 'existence is a perfection' premise Kant attacked, which the modal version deliberately avoids.
